stem: A hospitalized client says, 'My faith has been an important source of strength while I am sick.' Which nursing response best reflects client-centered spiritual care?

options.A: Tell me what spiritual support would be helpful to you. If you would like, I can help arrange a visit from a chaplain or your own clergy member.
options.B: Spiritual concerns are outside the nursing role, so I will focus only on your physical symptoms.
options.C: I will explain my own religious beliefs so you can decide whether they would help you cope better.
options.D: Spiritual care is appropriate only when the nurse and client share the same religious beliefs.

rationale: Open RN Nursing Fundamentals describes spiritual assessment and care as open, nonjudgmental, and centered on the client's own values and beliefs. Nurses should ask clients what they need to feel spiritually supported, accommodate requests when possible, and may offer referral to a chaplain or the client's clergy. Nurses should not promote their own beliefs. Therefore A is the best response; B excludes a legitimate nursing-care domain, while C and D substitute the nurse's beliefs for the client's values.
educational_objective: Provide client-centered spiritual care by assessing the client's own spiritual needs, supporting requested resources, and avoiding imposition of the nurse's personal beliefs.
source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf — Open Resources for Nursing (Open RN)
source_document_title: Nursing Fundamentals, 2nd edition — Part XVIII Spirituality
source_locator: Part XVIII > 18.2 Basic Concepts > Spiritual Assessment: ask what provides strength/hope and what spiritual needs can be advocated for; 18.4 Applying the Nursing Process / interventions: ask the client how the nurse can support them spiritually, offer chaplain/clergy resources, and support clients within their own faith tradition without promoting the nurse's beliefs
source_claim_supported: Spiritual care is part of holistic client-centered nursing; nurses assess spiritual needs nonjudgmentally, support the client's own values and beliefs, ask what support is desired, and can offer chaplain or clergy referral while avoiding promotion of their own belief system.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity, printed p.10/PDF p.14: Assess and support client coping, values, beliefs, cultural and spiritual practices; Promote a therapeutic environment
blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — spiritual needs, client values, and therapeutic support
correction_summary: Replaced the abstract statement that spirituality is 'an important source of meaning and coping' with an actionable nursing-response item. The corrected version directly tests client-centered spiritual assessment/support, permission-based chaplain or clergy referral, and avoidance of imposing the nurse's beliefs, all explicitly supported by current Open RN 2nd-edition content.

audit_findings.source_authority: PASS — NCBI/Open RN Nursing Fundamentals 2nd edition directly addresses spiritual assessment, nursing interventions, chaplain referral, and respect for client beliefs.
audit_findings.currentness: PASS — 2nd edition published 2024 and live NCBI page rechecked 2026-08-17.
audit_findings.exact_locator: PASS — Spiritual Assessment and nursing-intervention sections directly support the correct response and exclude imposition of nurse beliefs.
audit_findings.stem: PASS after correction — provides a concrete client cue and asks for the most therapeutic nursing response.
audit_findings.correct_answer: PASS — A asks what support the client wants and offers resources without assumption or coercion.
audit_findings.distractors: PASS — B wrongly excludes spiritual care; C imposes nurse beliefs; D falsely requires shared beliefs.
audit_findings.rationale: PASS — source-bound and avoids claiming that every client is religious or must accept chaplain services.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: PASS — only A is open, nonjudgmental, client-directed, and permission-based.
audit_findings.cueing: PASS — all choices are complete nursing responses; the key is not exposed by grammar or terminology.
audit_findings.blueprint: PASS — spiritual/cultural values and therapeutic support align with Psychosocial Integrity.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: PASS — independently re-read the source's spiritual-assessment questions, client-support interventions, chaplain referral guidance, and warning against promoting the nurse's beliefs; no second defensible answer remains.
